title: Implement AudioPipeline struct
description:
Create AudioPipeline struct - the main audio subsystem using single-pipe architecture.

Fields (per state-machine.md):
- buffers: Vec<StreamBuffer> - ring buffers for each channel (~3 seconds compressed audio)
- downloaders: Vec<DownloadHandle> - one download thread per channel
- decoder: Option<DecoderHandle> - single decoder thread (reads from active buffer)
- sink: Sink - single audio output (shared by decoder and TTS)
- active_channel: Option<usize> - which buffer decoder reads from
- _stream: OutputStream - keeps audio device alive

DecoderHandle should contain:
- thread: JoinHandle<()>
- stop_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>
- pause_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>

DownloadHandle should contain:
- thread: JoinHandle<()>
- stop_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>
- status: Arc<AtomicU8> (0=connecting, 1=playing, 2=error)

This replaces MultiStreamPlayer with single-pipe architecture.

title: Implement download error recovery with exponential backoff
description:
Add error recovery to download threads per state-machine.md Error Recovery section:
1. On connection failure, retry with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s)
2. While retrying, decoder continues playing from buffer (~3 seconds cushion)
3. If buffer empties during failure: signal main thread to announce 'Reconnecting...'
4. On success: seamless resume (buffer refills)
5. After 3 consecutive failures: mark stream unavailable, announce 'Station unavailable'
6. Track stream status via Arc<AtomicU8> (0=connecting, 1=playing, 2=error)

title: New state machine: Welcome → Playing → Browsing → Off
description: Replace current linear state machine with browse-then-commit UX. States: Welcome (blocking, auto-play ch0), Playing(channel), Browsing{playing, browse}, Off. Browse wraps through channels+Off. Commit trigger: TTS finishes + 0.5s grace. Stream stays playing ducked during browse, only switches on commit.
design:
## State Machine

```rust
enum RadioState {
    Welcome,
    Playing(usize),
    Browsing { playing: Option<usize>, browse: usize },
    Off,
}
```

Browse wraps channels only: 0 → 1 → ... → 12 → 0 (no Off position, long press = off)

## Transitions

**Welcome**: Boot → Hello → update check → Ready → auto-transition to Playing(0)

**Playing(channel)**: Stream at 100% on stream sink
- [short press] → Browsing { playing: channel, browse: (channel+1) % N }, duck stream to 20%, beep + TTS channel name, wait TTS end + 0.5s grace
- [long press] → stop stream → Off

**Browsing { playing, browse }**: Old stream KEEPS PLAYING at 20%
- [short press during TTS or grace] → interrupt TTS, browse = (browse+1) % N, beep + TTS new name, restart grace
- [TTS finishes + 0.5s, no press] → COMMIT: tri-tone, if browse == playing restore vol, else switch stream → Playing(browse)
- [long press] → stop stream → Off

**Off**: No stream
- [short press] → Browsing { playing: None, browse: 0 }, beep + TTS first channel
- [long press] → ignored

## Audio Architecture
Three sinks: stream (duckable), voice (TTS, interruptible), beep (independent)

## Example
Playing BBC Radio 4 → [press] → duck to 20% → beep → YLE Klassinen (wraps to 0) → [press] → beep → YLE Radio 1 → ... stops pressing ... → TTS finishes → 0.5s → tri-tone → switch stream

title: Fix duck timing for slow Piper TTS synthesis
description:
## Problem

On Raspberry Pi, Piper TTS synthesis takes 1-2 seconds. Current flow:

1. `speak()` called → `start_duck()` sets `duck_until = now + 1500ms`
2. Thread spawns → `tts.synthesize()` blocks for 1-2s
3. After synthesis → TTS audio plays

If synthesis takes 1500ms, the duck period expires BEFORE TTS audio starts.
Result: Channel announcements drowned out by stream.

## Solution

Move `start_duck()` call to AFTER `tts.synthesize()` completes, right before audio plays.

## Files to modify

- `src/audio.rs`: Pass `duck_until_ms` and `boot_time` to TTS thread, call `start_duck()` after synthesis

## Testing

Test on actual Pi hardware - verify TTS is audible over ducked stream.
close_reason: Refresh duck timer after Piper synthesis completes, before playing samples

title: Implement TTS integration with AudioPipeline
description:
Implement announce() method for TTS integration:

1. Pause decoder via pause_flag.store(true) - stops appending to sink
2. Synthesize speech with Piper (or Docker Piper on macOS)
3. Create SamplesBuffer from synthesized samples (mono, 22050 Hz)
4. Append to same sink used by decoder
5. Call sink.sleep_until_end() to block until TTS finishes
6. Resume decoder via pause_flag.store(false)

No muting/ducking needed - decoder simply pauses while TTS plays. The single sink handles both streams sequentially.

title: Implement MultiStreamPlayer struct


### StreamHandle struct
```rust
struct StreamHandle {
    thread: JoinHandle<()>,
    stop_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    sink: Arc<Mutex<Option<Sink>>>,  // For volume control from main thread

```

### MultiStreamPlayer struct
```rust
pub struct MultiStreamPlayer {
    _stream: OutputStream,
    stream_handle: OutputStreamHandle,
    streams: [Option<StreamHandle>; 4],
    active_index: Option<usize>,      // None = all muted (Off state)

```
